21:1: And these are the laws that you shall set before them.
AND these are the orders of judgments which thou shalt order before them.
21:2: If you buy a Hebrew slave [who is a son of a Hebrew], he shall serve [you] for six years, but in the seventh [year] he is to go out free, for naught [without liability].
If thou shalt have bought a son of Israel, on account of his theft, six years he shall serve, and at the incoming of the seventh he shall go out free without price.
21:3: If he came by himself [unmarried], he shall go out by himself. If he was married, his wife shall go out with him.
If he came in alone, he shall go out alone: but if (he be) the husband of a wife, a daughter of Israel, his wife shall go out with him.
21:4: If his master should give him a wife, and she bears him sons or daughters, then the woman and her children belong to her master, and he shall go out by himself.
If his master give him a wife, an handmaid, and she bear him sons or daughters, the wife and her children shall belong to his master, and he may go out alone.
21:5: If the slave explicitly says, “I have come to love my master, my wife and my children, I do not want to go out free.”
But if the servant shall affirm and say, I love my master, my wife, and my children, (and) I will not go out free,
21:6: His master must bring him to [before] the judges. He must then bring him next to the door, or to the doorpost, and his master shall pierce his ear with an awl. He then serves his master [will be a working servant for him,] forever.

then his master shall bring him before the judges, and shall receive from them the power, and bring him to the door that hath posts; and his master shall pierce his right ear with an awl; and he shall be a servant to serve him until the jubela.
21:7: If a man sells his daughter to be a maidservant, she shall not go out [free] in the manner of male slaves.

And if a man of Israel sell his daughter, a little handmaid, she shall not go forth according to the going forth of the servants of the Kenaanaee, who are set at liberty on account of the tooth or the eye; but in the years of remission, and with tokens, and at the jubela, and on the death of her master, and by redemption with money.
21:8: If she is displeasing to her master, who had not designated [for otherwise he would have designated] her as his wife, he must allow her to be redeemed. He has no power [right] to sell her to an alien people [another man] for he has dealt deceitfully with [controlled] her.

If she hath not found favour before her master who bought her, then her father may redeem her; but to a foreigner he shall not have power to sell her; for as a vessel of her Lord he hath power over her.
21:9: If he has designated her as a wife for his son, he must grant her exactly the same rights as daughters [of Yisrael].
And if he had intended her for the side of his son, he shall do by her after the manner of the daughters of Israel.
21:10: If he takes himself another [wife], her sustenance, her clothing and her conjugal rights he must not diminish.
If he take another daughter of Israel to him beside her, her food, her adorning, and her conjugal rights, he shall not withhold from her.
21:11: If he does not do these three things to her, she goes out free with no repayment of money.

And if these three things he doth not for her, to covenant her to himself, or to his son, or to release her into the hand of her father, she shall go free without payment, and a writing of release he shall give her.
21:12: If one strikes a man and he [the victim] dies, he shall be put to death.
Whosoever smiteth a son or a daughter of Israel, so as to cause death, shall be put to death with the sword.
21:13: But if he did not lie in wait [to ambush him] but [from before] God [he was] brought it to his hand, then I will designate for you a place, to which he can flee [and find refuge].
But he who did not attack him, but mischance from before the Lord befell him at his hand, I will appoint thee a place where he may flee.
21:14: But if a man plots against his neighbor to kill him intentionally, you may [even] take him from My altar to put him to death.
But if a man come maliciously upon his neighbour to kill him with craft, though the priests are ministering at My altar, thence thou shalt take him, and slay him with the sword.
21:15: Whoever strikes his father or his mother shall be put to death.
And he who woundeth his father or his mother shall die by strangling.
21:16: Whoever steals [kidnaps] a man [person from B’nei Yisrael] and sells him, if he is found in his hand, he shall be put to death.
And he who stealeth a soul of the children of Israel, and selleth him, or if he be found in his possession, shall die by strangling.
21:17: Whoever curses his father or his mother shall be put to death.
And he who curseth his father or his mother by the Great Name, dying he shall die by being stoned with stones.
21:18: When men quarrel and one man hits his fellow with a stone or with [his] fist; and he [the victim] does not die but becomes bedridden [falls to idleness],
And when men strive together, and one smite his neighbour with a stone, or with his fist, so that he die not, but fall ill,
21:19: If he gets up and is able to walk on the outside on his own power, the one who struck him shall be acquitted. Still he must pay for his loss of work, and must pay for his complete cure [the doctor’s fee].

if he rise again from his illness, and walk in the street upon his staff, he who smote him shall be acquitted from the penalty of death; only for his cessation from labour, his affliction, his injury, his disgrace, and the hire of the physician, he shall make good until he be cured.
21:20: If a man strikes his male or female slave with a rod [power], and [the slave] dies under his hand, [the death] must be avenged [judged].
And when a man hath smitten his Kenaanite man-servant or maid-servant with a staff, and he die the same day under his hand, he shall be judged with the judgment of death by the sword.
21:21: However if he [the slave] survives for a day or two, [his death] is not avenged [judged], for he [the slave] is his [master’s] property.
But if the wounded person continue one or two days from time to time, he shall not be (so) judged; because with money he had bought him.
21:22: If men will fight and they strike a pregnant woman, causing her to miscarry, but there is no fatal injury [to the woman], he [the guilty one] is to be punished with a [monetary] penalty when the husband demands compensation. He shall pay as determined by the judges.

If men when striving strike a woman with child, and cause her to miscarry, but not to lose her life, the fine on account of the infant which the husband of the woman shall lay upon him, he shall pay according to the sentence of the judges.
21:23: However if there is a fatal injury, you shall give [up] a life for a life.
But if death befall her, then thou shalt judge the life of the killer for the life of the woman.
21:24: [Compensation of] an eye for an eye, [of] a tooth for a tooth, [of] a hand for a hand, [of] a foot for a foot.
The value of an eye for an eye, the value of a tooth for a tooth, the value of a hand for a hand, the value of a foot for a foot,
21:25: [Compensation of] a burn for a burn, [of] a wound for a wound, [of] a bruise [beating] for a bruise [beating].
all equivalent of the pain of burning for burning, and of wounding for wounding, and of blow for blow.
21:26: If a man strikes the eye of his slave, or the eye of his female slave, and destroys [blinds] it, he shall set him [the slave] free as compensation for the eye.
And when a man strikes the eye of his Kenaanite servant or handmaid, and causeth blindness, he shall let him go free, on account of the eye.
21:27: If [he knocks out] the tooth of his slave, or knocks out the tooth of his female slave, he shall set him [the slave] free as compensation for the tooth.
And if he strike out the tooth of his Kenaanite man or maid-servant, he shall make the servant free on account of the tooth.
21:28: If an ox gores a man or woman and the victim dies, the ox shall be stoned [to death], and its flesh may not be eaten. The owner of the ox shall go unpunished.

And if an ox goreth a man or woman to cause death, the ox must be stoned, but shall not be killed that his flesh may be eaten; and the owner of the ox shall be exempt from the condemnation of death, and also from the price of the servant or handmaid.
21:29: But if the ox had gored yesterday and the day before, and a warning was given to its owner, but he had not taken proper precautions to guard it, and kills a man or a woman, the ox must be stoned, and the owner also shall die [by Divine decree].

But if the ox (had been wont) to gore yesterday and before, and it had been attested before his owner three times, and he (had neglected) to restrain him, the ox, when he killeth man or woman, shall be stoned, and his master also shall die with a death sent upon him from heaven.
21:30: When an atonement fine shall be imposed on him, he must give for the redemption of his soul whatever sum is imposed on him.
Yet if a fine of money be laid upon him, he may give a ransom for his life, according to what shall be imposed on him by the sanhedrin of Israel.
21:31: Whether it is a son [a minor lad] [of Yisrael] that is gored [by the ox] or a daughter [a minor girl] [of Yisrael] that it gored, this law shall apply to it.
Whether the ox hath gored a son or a daughter of Israel, according to that judgment it shall be done to him.
21:32: If the ox gored a male or female slave, he must give thirty silver shekalim [selaim] to their master, and the ox must be stoned.
If an ox goreth a Kenaanite man-servant or handmaid, the master of the man or woman-servant shall give thirty sileen of silver, and the ox shall be stoned.
21:33: If a man uncovers a pit, or if a man digs a pit, and does not cover it, and an ox or a donkey falls into it;
And if a man openeth a pit in the street, and doth not cover it, and an ox or an ass fall therein;
21:34: The owner of the pit must pay. He must compensate its owner with money, and the dead [animal] remains his [its original owner’s] possesion.
the master of the pit shall deliver silver to give to its owner the price of the ox or the ass, and the dead body shall be his.
21:35: If a man’s ox injures his neighbor’s ox and it dies, they shall sell the live ox and divide the money received for it. They shall also divide [the value of] the dead animal.
And when an ox woundeth his neighbour's ox, and he die, they shall sell the living ox, and divide the price, and the price of the dead one shall they also divide.
21:36: If it was known that it was a goring ox from yesterday and the day before, but he had not taken proper precaution to guard it, then he must pay full compensation, an ox for an ox. The dead [animal] remains in the possession [of its owner].
But if it hath been known that the ox was wont to gore in time past, and his master did not restrain him, he shall surely deliver ox for ox; but the carcase and the skin shall be his.
22:1: If a man steals an ox or a sheep, and then slaughters or sells it, he must pay five oxen for each ox, and four sheep for each sheep.

When a man stealeth an ox or a sheep, and killeth or selleth it, five oxen shall he make good for one ox, because he hath hindered him from his ploughing; and four sheep for one, because he hath impoverished him by his theft, and not done service by it.
22:2: If the thief is found [caught] while breaking in, and is struck and killed, there is no liability for his blood.
If a thief be found in a window of the wall, and be smitten and die, there shall not be on his account the guilt of the shedding of innocent blood.
22:3: If the sun shone on him [eyes of witnesses fell upon him], there is liability for his blood. He must make full restitution. If he does not have [the means to do so], he shall be sold [as a slave to pay] for his theft.

If the thing be as clear as the sun that he was not entering to destroy life, and one hath killed him, the guilt of the shedding of innocent blood is upon him; and if spared from his hand, restoring he shall restore. If he have not wherewith to restore, the beth din shall sell him for his theft until the year of release.
22:4: If the stolen article is found in his hand [possession], whether it is an ox, donkey or sheep [that is alive], he must pay two live animals.
If before witnesses, the thing stolen was found in his possession, from an ox or an ass, unto a sheep alive, he shall restore two for one.
22:5: If he damages a field or vineyard with his animal—he lets his livestock loose, and [or] it feeds in another’s field—from his [own] prime field and prime vineyard he must compensate [the owner].
If a man break in upon a field or a vineyard, and send in his beast to feed in another man's field, the best of his field and the best of his vineyard he shall restore.
22:6: If a fire goes out of control and finds [catches on] thorns, and then consumes bound or standing grain or a field, full restitution must be made by the one who started the fire.
If fire break out, and catch thorns, and consume the sheaves, or whatever is standing, or the field, whoever kindled the fire shall surely restore.
22:7: If a man gives his neighbor money or articles to safeguard and they are stolen from the house of the [watch]man, if the thief is found, he must pay double.
When a man confideth to his neighbour silver, or vessels to keep, without recompense for the care, and they be stolen from the man's house,
22:8: If the thief is not found, the owner of the house [the watchman] must come before the judges [Beis Din], [to swear] that he did not lay a hand on his neighbor’s possessions [for his personal use] [that which his neighbor handed over to him].

if the thief be found, he shall restore two for one. If the thief be not found, the master of the house shall be brought before the judges, and shall swear that he hath not put forth his own hand upon the property of his neighbour.
22:9: In every question of dishonesty whether it involves an ox, a donkey, a sheep, a garment, or anything that was [allegedly] lost of which [a witness] says, “This is it!” the claims of both parties must be brought to [before] the judges. The one whom the judges find guilty, must pay double restitution to his neighbor.

And about whatever is injured covertly, whether ox, or ass, or sheep, or raiment, of whatever is (so) lost, he shall make oath when he saith that so it is; and when the thing stolen shall be afterward found in the hand of the thief, the cause of both shall be brought before the judges, the cause of the householder and the cause of the thief; and whom the judges shall condemn, the thief shall restore twofold to his neighbour.
22:10: If a man gives his neighbor, a donkey, an ox, a sheep, or any animal for safeguarding; and it dies, or is injured, or is captured, and there is no eyewitness,

If a man deliver to his neighbour all ox, or a sheep, or any animal to keep, (if) he is to keep it without recompense, and it die, or be torn by wild beast, or be carried off, and no witness seeing who can testify it;
22:11: an oath to Adonoy shall be between them, that he [the watcher] did not lay his hand on his neighbor’s possession [for his personal use] [that which his neighbor handed over to him]. The owner must accept it [the oath], and [the watcher] need not make restitution.

an oath of the Lord shall be between them both, that he hath not put forth his hand upon the property of his neighbour; and the owner of the thing shall accept his oath, and he shall not (be required to) make it good.
22:12: But if it was indeed stolen from him, he must make restitution to its owner.
But if it be stolen from him who was to receive recompense for the care, he shall make it good to its owner.
22:13: If it was torn apart [killed by wild beasts], he [the watcher] must provide witnesses [that is was torn apart]. He then need not pay for that which was torn apart.
If it hath been torn by a wild beast, let him bring witnesses, or bring him to the carcase: because for that which is (so) torn he shall not make restitution.
22:14: If a man borrows something from his neighbor, and it becomes broken or dies; if the owner is not [involved] with him, he [the borrower] must make full restitution.
And if a man borrow anything of his neighbour, and the vessel be broken, or the animal die, and the owner be not with it, lie shall certainly make it good.
22:15: If the owner is [involved] with him, then he [the borrower] need not make restitution. If it was hired, it [the ox] comes in its rental price.
If the owner be with it, he shall not make it good: if it had been lent for profit, its loss came on account of its hire.
22:16: If a man seduces a virgin who is not betrothed, and lies with her; he must give the dowry to acquire [establish] her as his wife.
If a man seduce a virgin unbetrothed, and have criminal conduct with her, endowing, he shall endow her to be his wife.
22:17: If her father utterly refuses to give her to him, he must give [the father] the weight of silver equal to the dowry usually given to virgins.
If this doth not appear to him (to be desirable), or if her father be not willing to give her to him fifty sileen of silver shall be laid upon him, according to the endowment of a virgin.
22:18: You shall not allow a witch to live.
Sons of My people Israel, whosoever practiseth witchcraft you shall not suffer to live.
22:19: Whoever lies with an animal must be put to death.
Whosoever lieth with a beast shall be stoned to death.
22:20: Whoever slaughters to a god [false gods of the peoples] must be condemned [to die]. [Sacrifices may be offered] to [the Name of] Adonoy alone.
Whosoever sacrificeth to the idols of the Gentiles shall be slain with the sword, and his goods be destroyed; for ye shall worship only the Name of the Lord.
22:21: You must not abuse or oppress a stranger, for you were strangers in the land of Egypt.
And the stranger you shall not vex with words, nor distress him by taking his goods: Remember, sons of Israel, My people, that you were strangers in the land of Mizraim.
22:22: You must not mistreat any widow or orphan.
You shall not impoverish the widow or the orphan.
22:23: If you do mistreat him [them], when he cries out to [before] Me, I will indeed hear [obey] his cry.
If thou impoverish her, beware; for if they rise up and cry against you in prayer before Me, I will hear the voice of their prayer, and will avenge them,
22:24: Then I will cause My anger to flare, and I will kill you by the sword. Your wives will become widows and your children will be orphans.
and My anger will be kindled, and I will slay you with the sword, and your wives shall be widows, and your children be orphans.
22:25: When you lend money to My people, to the poor person who is with [among] you, do not act toward him as a [demanding] creditor. Do not place the burden of interest [an injury] upon him.

If thou lend money to (one of) My people, to (one of) the humble of My people, thou shalt not be to him as an usurer, neither lay it upon him that there shall be witnesses against him, or that he give pledges, or equivalents, or usury.
22:26: If you take your neighbor’s garment as security, you must return it to him till sunset;
If thou take (at all) for a pledge the garment of thy neighbour, thou shalt restore it to him before sunset;
22:27: For this alone is his covering, the garment [to cover] his skin. With what shall he lie down [to sleep]? If it happens that he cries out to [before] Me, I will hear [obey] [his cry] for I am gracious.

for it may be his taleth which alone covereth him; (or) it is his only garment in which he rests, which falleth upon his skin; and if thou take the coverlet of the bed whereon he lies, and he be heard before Me, I will hearken to his prayer; for I am Eloah the Merciful.
22:28: Do not curse judges. Do not curse a leader of your people.
Sons of Israel My people, ye shall not revile your judges, nor curse the rabbans who are appointed rulers among thy people.
22:29: [Your offering of] the fullness [of your newly ripened produce] and of your terumah-offering’s you must not delay. The first-born of your sons, you shall give to [separate before] Me.
The firsts of thy fruits, and the firsts of thy wine-press, thou shalt not delay to bring up in their time to the place of My habitation. The firstlings of thy males thou shalt separate before Me.
22:30: You must do likewise with your oxen and with your sheep. Seven days it shall remain with its mother. On the eighth day you must give it to [separate it before] Me.
So shalt thou do with the firstlings of thy oxen and sheep; seven days it shall be suckled by its mother, and on the eighth day thou shalt separate it before Me.
22:31: You shall be men of holiness to [before] Me, and you must not eat flesh that was torn off in the field [from a living animal]. Throw it to the dog.
And holy men, tasting unconsecrated things innocently, shall you be before Me; but flesh torn by wild beasts alive you may not eat, but throw it to the dog as his portion.
23:1: Do not accept a false report. Do not join hands with a wicked man to be a corrupt [false] witness [for him].
Sons of Israel My people, take not up lying words from a man who accuseth his neighbour before thee, nor put thine hand with the wicked to become a false witness.
23:2: Do not follow the majority to do evil. Do not respond with your opinion in a dispute [merely] to lean [toward one side] [(Do not) refrain from teaching what is proper in your eyes regarding a judgment]. It must be decided by the majority.

Sons of Israel My people, you shall not go after the many to do evil, but to do good; and no one among you shall restrain himself from affirming justly concerning his neighbour in the judgment, by saying, Behold, the judgment sides with the many.
23:3: Do not show favor [even] to the poor in his dispute [judgment].
And to the poor man who is guilty in his cause, thou shalt not be partial in having compassion upon him; for there must not be respect of persons in judgment.
23:4: If you come across your enemy’s ox or his donkey going astray, bring it back to him.
If thou meet the ox of thine enemy whom thou dislikest on account of the wickedness which thou only knowest is in him, or an ass that wandereth from the way, thou shalt surely bring it to him.
23:5: If you see the donkey of your enemy lying under its burden, and you might not want to help him [stop yourself from abandoning him], [but you should] [[you should]] make every effort to help him [abandon what is in you heart against him and unload with him] .

If thou seest the ass of thy enemy whom thou dislikest on account of the wickedness which thou only knowest to be in him, lying under his burden, and thou wouldst refrain thyself from going near him, thou shalt relinquish at once the dislike of thy heart against (thy enemy), and release and take care of the ass (or, charge thyself with him).
23:6: Do not bend justice [even] for your needy in his dispute.
Sons of Israel My people, ye shall not warp the judgment of the poor in his cause.
23:7: Keep far away from anything false. Do not kill an [one who is] innocent [or one who goes out innocent from judgment] righteous man, for I will not acquit a wicked person.

From a false matter keep distant. And when one hath gone forth from thy house of justice acquitted, and they (afterwards) find out his guilt; or one hath been brought out condemned, and they (afterward) find out his innocence,-­thou shalt not put him to death; for I will not hold (the former) innocent, nor the latter guilty.
23:8: Do not accept bribery, for bribery blinds the clear-sighted [eyes of the wise], and perverts the words of justice.

And thou mayest not receive a bribe; for a bribe blindeth their eyes who have taken it, and casteth down the wise from their seats, and perverteth the right words which are written in the law, and confoundeth the words that are in the mouth of the innocent in the hour of judgment.
23:9: Do not oppress a stranger. You [should] know the soul [feelings] of the stranger, for you were strangers in the land of Egypt.
Thou shalt not oppress the stranger; for ye know the sigh of a stranger's soul; because ye were sojourners in the land of Mizraim.
23:10: You may sow your land for six years, and gather its crops.
Six years thou shalt sow thy land, and gather the produce;
23:11: But on the seventh [year] you must let it rest, and abandon it [by not eating its produce], and let the needy among your people eat it. What they leave over, the beasts of the field can eat. Do the same with your vineyard and your olive [trees].

but the seventh year thou shalt exempt it from labour, and give up the fruit of it to be eaten by the poor of My people; and what they leave shall be eaten by the beasts of the field. And in like manner shalt thou do with thy vine and olive grounds.
23:12: You may do your work six days, but on the seventh day you must cease; so that your ox and your donkey may rest, and the son of your female slave may be refreshed, and [also] the stranger.
Six days do thy work, and on the seventh day repose, that thy ox and thy ass may rest, and that the uncircumcised son of thy handmaid, and the stranger, may rest.
23:13: Preserve everything that I have said to you. Do not mention the name of other [false] gods [of the peoples]. You must not cause it to be heard through your mouth.
And of all the precepts that I have spoken to you, be carefull; and the names of the idols of the Gentiles remember not, nor let them be heard upon your lips.
23:14: Three times a year you are to celebrate with [before] Me.
Three times in the year thou shalt keep festival before Me.
23:15: You must keep the festival of Matzos. You must eat matzos for seven days, as I have commanded you. [This festival must be celebrated] at the appointed time, during the month when the grain is ripened, for in it [at this time] you went out of Egypt. Do not appear before My Presence [Me] empty-handed.

The feast of unleavened cakes thou shalt keep. Seven days thou art to eat unleavened bread, as I have instructed thee, in the time of the month of Abiba, because in it thou camest forth from Mizraim; and you shall not appear before Me empty.
23:16: [You must also keep] the Festival of Harvest, [with bringing bikurim] the first fruits of your labor, which you planted in the field; [also] the Festival of Ingathering, at the close of the year, when you gather in [the fruits of] your labor from the field.
And the feast of the harvest first-fruits of the work thou didst sow in the field; and the feast of gathering, at the end of the year, when thou hast gathered in thy work from the field.
23:17: Three times a year, every male among you must appear before the Presence of the Master [of the world], Adonoy.
Three times in the year shall all thy males appear before the Lord the Ruler of the world.
23:18: You must not sacrifice—while chometz is present—My [Pesach] sacrifice. You must not allow to remain overnight [off the Altar]—the fat[s] of My [the] festival-offering—until morning.

Sons of Israel My people, while there is leaven in your houses you may not immolate the bloody sacrifice of My Pascha; nor shall the fat of the sacrifice of My Pascha remain without the altar until morning, nor of the flesh that you eat in the evening.
23:19: The beginning of the first fruits of your land must be brought to the House of [the Sanctuary of] Adonoy, your God. You must not cook a young animal in the milk of its mother [eat meat with milk].

The first of the choice fruits of thy ground thou shalt bring to the sanctuary of the Lord thy God. My people of the house of Israel, you are not permitted to dress or to eat of flesh and milk mingled together, lest I be greatly displeased; and I prepare you the wheat and the straw together for your food.
23:20: Behold, I will send an angel before you, to guard you on the way, and to bring you to the place that I have prepared.
Behold, I will send an Angel before thee, to keep thee in the way, and to bring thee in to the place of My habitation which I have prepared.
23:21: Be careful in his presence and heed [obey] his voice [word]. Do not rebel against him; for he cannot bear [pardon] your transgression, as [in] My Name is in him [his word].
Be circumspect before Him, and obey His word, and be not rebellious against His words; for He will not forgive your sins, because His word is in My Name.
23:22: But if you truly listen to [obey] his voice [word], and do all that I speak, then I will be an enemy to your enemies, and attack those who attack you.
For if thou wilt indeed hearken to His Word, and do all that I speak by Him, I will be the enemy of thy enemy, and will trouble them who trouble thee.
23:23: My messenger will go before you, and will bring you into [the land of] the Emorites, the Chittites, the Perizzites, the Canaanites, Chivites, and the Yevusites, and I will then annihilate them.
For My Angel shall go before thee, and bring thee to the Amoraee, and Pherizaee, and Kenaanaee, Hivaee, and Jebusaee; and I will destroy them.
23:24: You must not prostrate yourself to their [false] gods, nor serve [sacrifice to] them. You must not adopt their customs. You must totally destroy [their idols] and completely break down their monuments.
Thou shalt not worship their idols, nor serve them, nor do after their evil works; but thou shalt utterly demolish the house of their worship, and break the statues of their images.
23:25: You must serve [before] Adonoy, your God, and He will bless your bread [food] and your water [drink]. I will eliminate [bad] sickness from your midst.
And you shall do service before the Lord our God and He will bless the provision of thy food and thy drinks, and remove the bitter plague from among thee.
23:26: No woman will suffer miscarriage or remain childless in your land. I will cause the number of your days to be full.
None shall be abortive or barren in thy land; the number of the days of thy life I will fulfil from day to day.
23:27: I will send My dread ahead of you, and I will bring panic to all the people among whom you will come [to fight against]. I will make all your enemies turn their backs to [before] you.
My terror will I send before thee, and will perturb all the peoples to whom thou comest, that thou mayest wage battle against them; and I will make all thy enemies turn back before thee.
23:28: I will send [deadly] hornets ahead of you, and they will drive out the Chivites, the Canaanites, and the Chittites from before you.
And I will send the hornet before thee to drive out the Hivaee, and Kenaanaee, and Hitaee, from before thee.
23:29: I will not drive them out in a single year, lest the land become desolate, and the beasts of the field multiply against you.
I will not expel them before thee in one year, lest the land become a wilderness, and the beasts of the field multiply upon thee, when they come to eat their carcasses, and injure thee.
23:30: Little by little I will drive them from before you, until you have increased and occupy the land.
By little and little I will drive them out before thee, until thou art increased, and inherit the land.
23:31: I will set your borders from the Reed Sea to the Philistine Sea, and from the desert to the [Euphrates] river, for I will deliver into your hands all the inhabitants of the land, and you will drive them away before you.

And I will set thy boundary from the sea of Suph, to the sea of the Philistaee, and from the desert unto the Pherat; for I will deliver into your hand all the inhabitants of the land, and thou shalt drive them out from before thee.
23:32: Do not make a pact with them or with their [false] gods.
Thou shalt make no covenant with them, nor with their idols.
23:33: Do not allow them to live in your land, since they may cause you to sin to [before] Me; that you [might] worship their [false] gods, and this would be a [fatal] trap to you.
Thou shalt not let them dwell in thy land, lest they cause thee to err, and to sin before Me, when thou dost worship their idols; for they will be a stumbling-block to thee.
24:1: He [God] had said to Moshe, ‘Go up to [the Presence of] [before] Adonoy, you, Aharon, Nadav, Avihu, and seventy of the elders of [the B’nei] Yisrael, and prostrate yourselves at a distance.

And Michael, the Prince of Wisdom, said to Mosheh on the seventh day of the month, Come up before the Lord, thou and Aharon, Nadab and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel, and worship at a distance.
24:2: Moshe alone shall approach [the Presence of] [before] Adonoy, but they must not approach, and the people must not go up with him.”
And Mosheh alone shall approach before the Lord; but they shall not draw nigh, nor may the people come up with him.
24:3: Moshe came and told the people all the words of Adonoy, and all the laws. The people responded with one voice and said, “All the words that Adonoy has spoken, we will do.”
And Mosheh came and set before the people all the words of the Lord, and all the judgments. And all the people answered with one voice, and said, All that the Lord hath spoken we will do.
24:4: Moshe wrote down all the words of Adonoy. He arose early in the morning, and built an altar beneath [at the foot of] the mountain, and [also] twelve monuments [pillars] for the twelve tribes of [the B’nei] Yisrael.
And Mosheh wrote the words of the Lord, and arose in the morning and builded an altar at the lower part of the mountain; and twelve pillars for the twelve tribes of Israel.
24:5: He sent the youths [first-born] of B’nei Yisrael and they offered burnt-offerings, and sacrificed oxen as peace-offerings to [before] Adonoy.

And he sent the firstborn of the sons of Israel,-for until that hour had the firstborn had the (office of performing) worship, the tabernacle of ordinance not (as yet) being made, nor the priesthood given unto Aharon; and they offered burnt offerings and consecrated oblations of oxen before the Lord.
24:6: Moshe took half the blood and put it in the basins, and [the other] half the blood he sprinkled on the altar.
And Mosheh took half of the blood of the offering, and put it in basins, and half of the blood of the offering he sprinkled upon the altar.
24:7: He then took the Book of the Covenant, and read it in the ears of [before] the people. They said, “All that Adonoy has spoken, we will do and we will listen [obey].”
And he took the Book of the Covenant of the Law and read before the people; and they said, All the words which the Lord hath spoken we will perform and obey.
24:8: Moshe then took the blood and cast it on the [Altar to atone on behalf of the] people, and he said, “Behold, this is the blood of the covenant which Adonoy has made with you regarding all these words.”

And Mosheh took half of the blood which was in the basins, and sprinkled upon the altar, to expiate the people, and said, Behold, this is the blood of the Covenant which the Lord hath made with you upon all these words.
24:9: Moshe and Aharon then went up along with Nadav and Avihu, and seventy of the elders of [the B’nei] Yisrael.
And Mosheh and Aharon, Nadab and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel, went up.
24:10: They saw [a vision of] the [Glory of the] God of Yisrael, and under His feet [the throne of His Glory] [there was something] like a brickwork of sapphire [precious stone], and it was like the essence [image] of heaven in purity.

And Nadab and Abihu lifted up their eyes, and saw the glory of the God of Israel; and under the footstool of His feet which was placed beneath His throne, was like the work of sapphire stone a memorial of the servitude with which the Mizraee had made the children of Israel to serve in clay and bricks, (what time) there were women treading clay with their husbands; the delicate young woman with child was also there, and made abortive by being beaten down with the clay. And thereof did Gabriel, descending, make brick, and, going up to the heavens on high, set it, a footstool under the cathedra of the Lord of the world whose splendour was as the work of a precious stone, and as the power of the beauty of the heavens when they are clear from clouds.
24:11: But against the nobility of the B’nei Yisrael, He [God] did not send His hand [there was no damage]. They envisioned [saw the Glory of] God, and they [rejoiced in their sacrifices which were accepted graciously as if they] ate and drank.

But upon Nadab and Abihu, the comely young men, was the stroke not sent in that hour, but it awaited them on the eighth day for a retribution to destroy them; but they saw the glory of the Shekinah of the Lord, and rejoiced that their oblations were received with favour, [as if they] did eat and drink.
24:12: Adonoy then said to Moshe, “Come up to [before] Me to the mountain and remain there. I will give you the tablets of stone, the Torah and the commandment, which I have written [in order] to teach them.”

And the Lord said to Mosheh, Ascend before Me at the mount, and I will there give thee the tables of stone on which I have set forth the rest of the words of the Law, and the six hundred and thirteen precepts which I have written for their instruction.
24:13: Moshe and Yehoshua, his attendant, set out, but [only] Moshe went up to the mountain [upon which the Glory] of God [was revealed].
And Mosheh arose and Jehoshua his minister; and Mosheh went up to the mountain on which was revealed the glory of the Shekinah of the Lord.
24:14: He [Moshe] said to the elders, “Wait here for us until we return to you, and Aharon and Chur will be with you. Whoever has a claim can approach [before] them.”
And to the sages he had said, Expect us here, at the time of our return to you; and, behold, Aharon and Hur are with you; if there be any matter of judgment, bring it to them.
24:15: Moshe went up to the mountain, and the cloud covered the mountain.
And Mosheh went up into the mount, and the Cloud of Glory covered the mount.
24:16: The glory of Adonoy rested on Mount Sinai, and the cloud covered it for six days. On the seventh day, He called to Moshe from the midst of the cloud.
And the glory of the Lord's Shekinah abode upon the mountain of Sinai, and the Cloud of Glory covered it six days. And on the seventh day He called to Mosheh from the midst of the Cloud.
24:17: The appearance of Adonoy’s glory was like [the appearance of] a consuming flame at the top to the mountain; before the eyes of the B’nei Yisrael.
And the appearance of the splendour of the glory of the Lord was as burning fire with flashes of devouring fire; and the sons of Israel beheld and were awe-struck.
24:18: And Moshe came into the midst of the cloud. and went up into the mountain. Moshe remained on the mountain for forty days and forty nights.

And Mosheh entered into the midst of the Cloud, and ascended the mountain; and Mosheh was upon the mountain forty days and forty nights, learning the words of the Law from the mouth of the Holy One, whose Name be praised.
25:1: And the Lord spake with Mosheh, saying,
25:2: Speak to the B’nei Yisrael and have them take for [separate before] Me a terumah-offering. From every man whose heart impels him to generosity shall you take My terumah-offering.
Speak unto the children of Israel, that they shall set apart (take) before me a Separation: of every one whose heart is willing, but not by constraint, ye shall take my separation.
25:3: This is the terumah-offering that you shall take from them: gold, silver and copper.
And this is the separation which you shall take of them: gold, and silver, and brass;
25:4: Greenish-blue [wool], dark red [wool], crimson [colored] [wool], fine linen, and goats [hair].
and hyacinth, and purple, and crimson, and fine linen; and goats' skins,
25:5: Red[-dyed] ram’s skins, tachash [multicolored] skins, and acacia wood.
and skins of rams dyed red, and purpled skins, and woods of sittin,
25:6: Oil for the lamp. Spices for anointing-oil, and for the incense of aromatic spices.
and olive oil for the light, and aromatics for the confection of the pure anointing oil, and of the fragrant incense;
25:7: Onyx stones, and filling stones [for setting] [into] the eiphod and breastplate.
gems of beryl that are gems of perfection, for engraving and insertion in the ephoda and in the breastplate.
25:8: They shall make a Sanctuary for [before] Me, and I will [then] dwell in their midst [rest My Shechina among them].
And they shall make a Sanctuary to My Name, that My Shekinah may dwell among them.
25:9: According to all that I am showing you—the form of the mishkon [tabernacle] and the form of all its vessels—and so should you make [it].
According to all that I show thee, the likeness of the tabernacle and the likeness of all its vessels, so shalt thou make.
25:10: They shall make an ark of acacia wood, two and one-half amohs long, one and one-half amohs wide, and one and one-half amohs high.
And they shall make an ark of sitta wood; two cubits and a half its length, a cubit and a half its breadth, and a cubit and a half its height.
25:11: Cover it with pure gold—you shall cover it inside and out. Make for it a golden crown-like rim around [its top].
And thou shalt cover it with pure gold within and without, and shalt make upon it a crown of gold round about.
25:12: Cast four gold rings, and place them on its [the ark’s] four corners, two rings on one side, and two rings on the second side.
And thou shalt cast for it four rings of gold, and set them upon its four corners; two rings for one side, and two rings for the second side.
25:13: Make [two] poles of acacia wood, and cover them with gold.
And thou shalt make staves of sitta wood, and cover them with gold;
25:14: Place the poles in the rings on the sides of the ark, so that the ark can be carried with them.
and thou shalt introduce the staves into the rings on the sides of the ark, that the ark may be carried upon them.
25:15: In the rings of the ark, must the poles remain. They must not be removed from them.
The staves shall be inlaid in the rings of the ark, and not be removed from it.
25:16: You shall then place in the ark, the Testimony that I will give you.
And thou shalt put within the ark the Testament that I will give thee.
25:17: Make a cover of pure gold [for the ark], two and one-half amohs long, and one and one-half amohs wide.
And thou shalt make a (kaphortha) mercy-seat of pure gold; two cubits and a half the length, and a cubit and a half the breadth, and its depth shall be a handbreadth (pusheka).
25:18: Make two golden cherubim. You must make them by hammering them out of the two ends of the [ark] cover.
And thou shalt make two kerubin, of pure beaten gold shalt thou make them on the two sides of the mercy-seat.
25:19: Make one cherub out of one end [side], and one cherub out of the other end [side]. From the [same piece of gold as] the cover itself, you shall make the cherubim on its two ends [sides].
Thou shalt make one keruba on this side, and one keruba on that side of the mercy-seat; you shall make the kerubaia on its two sides.
25:20: The cherubim shall spread their wings upward, sheltering the cover with their wings, and the cherubim shall face one another. Their faces shall be [inclined] toward the cover.

And the kerubaia shall stretch forth their wings above, their heads over against each other, their wings overshadowing the mercy-seat, and their faces over against each other; towards the mercy-seat shall be the faces of the kerubaia.
25:21: Place the cover on top of the ark and place the Testimony in the ark that I will give you.
And thou shalt put the mercy-seat above upon the ark, and within the ark thou shalt lay the Tables of the Testament that I will give thee.
25:22: I will set [prepare] My meetings [Word] with you there, and I will speak with you from above the cover, from between the cherubim that are on the Ark of the Testimony. All that which I will command you concerning the B’nei Yisrael.

And I will appoint My Word with thee there, and will speak with thee from above the mercy-seat, between the two kerubaia that are over the ark of the testament, concerning all that I may command thee for the sons of Israel.
25:23: You shall make a table out of acacia wood, two amohs will be its length, one amoh will be its width, and one and one-half amohs its height.
And thou shalt make a table of sitta wood; two cubits its length, and a cubit its breadth, and a cubit and a half its height.
25:24: Overlay it with pure gold, and make a gold crown-like rim around it.
And thou shalt overlay it with pure gold, and make for it a rim of gold round about.
25:25: Make a ledge of a tefach [high] around [the table], and make a gold crown-like rim around the ledge.
And thou shalt make to it a border, a handbreadth high round about, and make a golden wreath for its border round about.
25:26: Make four gold rings [for the table], and place the rings on the four corners that are on its legs.
And thou shalt make for it four golden rings, and set the rings in its four corners which are at its four feet.
25:27: The rings shall be against the ledge, and they shall be houses [receptacles] for the poles with which to carry the table.
Over against the border shall the rings be, for the place of the staves, to carry the table.
25:28: Make the poles out of acacia wood, and overlay them with gold. The table will be carried by them.
25:29: Make its dishes [bread forms], spoons, its half-hollow tubes, and its supports, by which they [the breads] shall be covered. Make them out of pure gold.
And thou shalt make its dishes and its spoons, its tankards and its measures, which are for the service of libation; of pure gold shalt thou make them.
25:30: You shall place the showbread upon the table, before Me at all times.
And upon the table thou shalt set in order the interior bread before Me continually.
25:31: You shall make a menorah [out] of pure gold. The menorah must be made by hammering [its form out of a solid piece of gold]. Its base, its shaft, its cups, its knobs, and its flowers shall be of it [the same piece of gold].
And thou shalt make a Candelabrum; of pure beaten gold shalt thou make the candelabrum; its base and shaft, its cups and apples and lilies, shall be of the same.
25:32: Six branches shall extend from its sides, three branches of the menorah from one of its sides, and three branches of the menorah from the second side.
Six branches shall spread out from its sides; three branches of the candelabrum from one side, and three branches of the candelabrum on the second side.
25:33: Three cups, engraved in almond shaped patterns, on one branch, with a knob and a flower. And three cups engraved in almond shaped patterns, on one branch, with a knob and a flower. So shall be [the form] of each of the six branches that extend from [the shaft of] the menorah.

Three calyxes adorned with their figurations on one branch, with apple and lily; and three calyxes adorned with their figurations on the other branch, with apple and lily: so for the six branches that spread out from the candelabrum.
25:34: The [shaft of the] menorah shall have four cups, engraved in almond shaped patterns, with their knobs and their flowers.
And upon the candelabrum there shall be four calyxes adorned with their figurations, their apples and lilies.
25:35: [There shall be] a knob under the two branches extending from it. [There should be] a [second] knob under the [second] two branches extending from it. [There should be] a [third] knob under the [third] two branches extending from it. [This holds true] for the six branches that extend from [the shaft of] the menorah.
And there shall be an apple under two branches of it, and an apple under two branches of it, and an apple under two branches of it, for the six branches which extend from the candelabrum.
25:36: Their knobs and their branches shall be made out of [the menorah] itself. It shall all be made of a single hammered work of pure gold.
Their apples and their branches shall be of the same; all of it one beaten work of pure gold.
25:37: You shall make seven lamps [for the menorah]. and its lamps shall be lit so that they shine toward it [the center lamp].
And thou shalt make its seven lights, and the priest who ministers shall kindle the lights, that they may shine over upon its face.
25:38: Its tongs and its [ash] scoops [shall also be made of] pure gold.
And its snuffers and its shovels of pure gold.
25:39: It shall be made out of a kikar of pure gold [together] with all these vessels.
Of a talent of pure gold shall he make it and all these its vessels.
25:40: Observe [carefully] and make them like the pattern that will be shown to you on the mountain.
And look thou, and make according to their forms which thou hast seen in the mount.
26:1: You shall [then] make the mishkon (Tabernacle) out of ten drapes, [consisting of] fine twined linen, greenish blue, dark red and crimson [colored] [wool]. Figures of cherubim, the work of a craftsman, shall be woven into them.
And the Tabernacle thou shalt make with ten curtains of fine linen twined, and hyacinth, and purple, and crimson, with figures of kerubin; with the work of the artificer shalt thou make them.
26:2: Each drape shall be twenty eight amohs long, and each drape shall be four amohs wide. All the drapes shall have the same measure.
The length of one curtain twenty and eight cubits, and the breadth of one curtain four cubits; the measure of one shall be that of all the curtains.
26:3: Five of these drapes shall be joined [sewn] together and [the other] five drapes shall be joined [sewn] together.
Five curtains shall be coupled one with another, and five other curtains coupled one with another.
26:4: Make loops of greenish blue [wool] on the edge of the drape which is at the [innermost] end of the [first] group. Do the same on the edge of the drape which is at the [innermost] end of the second group.
And thou shalt make loops of hyacinth upon the edge of one curtain at the side in the place of coupling, and so shalt thou do in the edge of the second curtain in the place of conjoinment.
26:5: Make fifty loops on [the edge of] one drape, and make fifty loops on the edge of the drape which is on the second group. The loops shall be opposite one another.
Fifty loops shalt thou make in one curtain, and fifty loops shalt thou make in the side of the second curtain in the place of conjoinment, so that the loops may answer one to the other.
26:6: Make fifty golden clasps, and join the drapes [of each group] together with the clasps, so that the mishkon is one.
And thou shalt make fifty taches of gold, and couple the curtains one with another with the taches, and the Tabernacle shall be conjoined to be one.
26:7: Make drapes of goats hair for a covering over the mishkon. Make eleven drapes.
And thou shalt make curtains of goats' hair to extend over the tabernacle: eleven curtains thou shalt make them.
26:8: The length of each drape shall be thirty amohs, and the width of each drape shall be four amohs. The eleven drapes must have the same measure.
The length of one curtain thirty cubits, and the breadth of one curtain four cubits; and the measure of one (shall be that of each) of the eleven (other) curtains.
26:9: Join [sew] together five drapes by themselves, and [the other] six drapes by themselves. Let the sixth drape overhang before the entrance of the tent [mishkon].

And thou shalt conjoin five curtains together, corresponding with the five books of the Law; and six curtains together, corresponding with the six orders of the Mishna; and shalt fold the sixth curtain over the front of the tabernacle.
26:10: Make fifty loops on the edge of one drape which is at the [innermost] end of the [first] group, and fifty loops on the edge of the drape which is on the second group.
And thou shalt make fifty loops upon the edge of one curtain at the side of the place of coupling; and fifty loops in the edge of the second curtain at the place of coupling.
26:11: Make fifty copper clasps. Bring the clasps into the loops, and join the tent together, making it one.
And thou shalt make taches of brass, fifty, and put the taches into the loops, and conjoin the tabernacle, that it may be one.
26:12: The overlapping excess [from what is left over] [in the breadth] of the drapes of the tent—half of the extra drape shall overlap the back of the mishkon.
And the surplus which remaineth of the curtains of the Tabernacle, the half curtain which remaineth, thou shalt spread over the hinder part of the Tabernacle.
26:13: The [extra] amoh on one side, and the [extra] amoh on the other side that were in excess of the length of the drapes of the tent shall overlap the sides of the mishkon, on both sides, to cover it.
And the cubit here and the cubit there, of that which remaineth in the curtains of the tabernacle, shall hang over the sides of the tabernacle here and there, to cover it.
26:14: Make a covering for the tent out of red dyed ram’s skins, and a covering of tachash [multicolored] skins above that.
And thou shalt make a covering for the tabernacle of rams' skins dyed red, and a covering of purple skins above.
26:15: Make the planks for the mishkon out of acacia wood; [these planks are] to stand upright [vertically].
And thou shalt make the boards of the tabernacle of sittin woods; they shall stand up, after the manner of their plantation.
26:16: Each plank shall be ten amohs long, and one and one half amohs shall be the width of each plank.
Ten cubits the length of the board, and a cubit and a half the breadth of one board.
26:17: Each plank shall have two [square] pegs, exactly parallel to each other. So shall you make all the planks of the mishkon.
Two tenons to one board, each in its side answering to the other: so shalt thou do for all the boards of the tabernacle.
26:18: Make these planks for the mishkon, twenty planks for the southern side.
And thou shalt make the boards of the tabernacle, twenty boards towards the wind on the south side.
26:19: Make forty silver sockets, [and place them] under the twenty planks. There shall be two sockets under one plank [one] for each of the two pegs, and two sockets under the other plank, [one] for each of the two pegs.
And thou shalt make forty bases of silver beneath the twenty boards; two bases beneath one board with its two tenons, and two bases under the other board with its two tenons.
26:20: For the second wall of the mishkon, to the northern side, [also make] twenty planks.
And for the second side of the tabernacle towards the north wind twenty boards,
26:21: [Make] their forty silver sockets, two sockets under each plank, two sockets under each plank.
and their forty bases of silver; two bases under one, and two bases under the other board.
26:22: For the west end of the mishkon make six planks.
And for the side of the tabernacle westward thou shalt make six boards.
26:23: Make two planks for the corners of the mishkon at the rear side [their ends].
And two boards shalt thou make at the corners of the tabernacle at their ends.
26:24: They must be coupled together on the bottom, and they must also be coupled together evenly on the top with one [square] ring. So must it be done with the two [planks], which are at the two corners.
And they shall be conjoined beneath, and in one manner shall be conjoined at their heads, with one ring; so shall it be with them both; for the two corners shall all they be.
26:25: Thus there will be eight planks, and their silver sockets, totaling sixteen sockets, two sockets under each plank, two sockets under each plank.
And there shall be eight boards and their silver bases; sixteen bases; two bases under one board, and two bases under another board.
26:26: You shall make bars out of acacia wood, five for the planks of one wall,
And thou shalt make bars of sittin woods, five for the boards of one side of the tabernacle,
26:27: and five bars for the planks of the second wall of the mishkon. [There shall also be] five bars for the planks of the western [back] wall of the mishkon.
and five bars for the boards of the second side of the tabernacle, and five bars for the side of the tabernacle at their extremity towards the west,
26:28: The middle [center] bar shall go through the planks, reinforcing the planks from one end to the other.

And the middle bar in the midst of the boards passing from end to end shall be from the tree which Abraham planted in Beara of Sheba: for when Israel had crossed the sea, the angels cut down the tree and cast it into the sea, and it floated on the face of the waters. And an angel proclaimed, and said, This is the tree which Abraham planted in Beara of Sheba, and prayed there in the name of the Word of the Lord. And the sons of Israel shall take and make thereof the middle bar, seventy cubits in length, and with it shall wondrous things be done: for when they have reared up the tabernacle, it shall go round it like a serpent among the boards of the tabernacle and when they take it down, it shall become straight as a rod.
26:29: You shall overlay the planks with gold, and make their rings out of gold, to hold the bars. You shall [also] overlay the bars with gold.
And the boards thou shalt overlay with gold, and make of gold their rings for the place of the bars, and shalt overlay the bars with gold.
26:30: You shall erect the mishkon according to its rules. As shown to you on the mountain.
And thou shalt rear the tabernacle according to the manner showed thee in the mountain.
26:31: You shall make a paroches [partition] out of greenish blue wool, dark red wool, crimson [colored] wool, and twined, fine linen. It shall be the work of a craftsman, with figures of cherubim [woven into it].
And thou shalt make a veil of hyacinth, and purple, and crimson, and fine linen entwined; the work of the artificer shalt thou make it, with figures of kerubin.
26:32: Place it [the paroches] upon four acacia-wood pillars, that are overlaid with gold. Their hooks shall [also] be of gold. These pillars are to be set into four silver sockets.
And thou shalt range it upon four pillars of sitta, covered with gold, their hooks of gold, upon four bases of silver.
26:33: Place the paroches under the clasps [which kept the drapes together]. Bring into the space within [behind] the paroches, the Ark of the Testimony, and the paroches will divide for you between the Holy and the Holy of Holies.
And thou shalt place the veil under the taches, and bring in thither within the veil the ark of the testament: and thou shalt spread the veil for you between the Holy and the Holy of Holies.
26:34: Place the cover upon the Ark of the Testimony in the Holy of Holies.
And thou shalt place the mercy-seat with the kerubaia produced of beaten work for it in the Holy of Holies.
26:35: Put the table outside the paroches, and the menorah opposite the table, toward the southern side of the mishkon. The table should be placed on the northern side.
And thou shalt set the Table outside of the veil, and the Candelabrum over against the table on the southern side of the tabernacle; but the table thou shalt arrange on the northern side.
26:36: You shall make a screen for the entrance of the tent. [Make it out of] greenish blue wool, dark red wool, crimson [colored] wool, and twined, fine linen. It shall be the work of an embroiderer.
And thou shalt make a curtain for the door of the tabernacle, of hyacinth, purple, and crimson, and fine linen twined, the work of the embroiderer.
26:37: Make five pillars of acacia wood for the screen. Overlay them with gold and their hooks are to be gold. Cast five copper sockets for them [the pillars].
And thou shalt make for the curtain five pillars of sitta, and cover them with gold, and their nails shall be of gold; and thou shalt cast for them five bases of brass.
27:1: You shall make the altar out of acacia wood. It shall be five amohs long, and five amohs wide. The altar shall be square, and its height shall be three amohs.
And thou shalt make the Altar of woods of sitta; five cubits the length, and five cubits the breadth: square shall be the altar, and its height three cubits.
27:2: Make its raised projections on its four corners. Its raised projections shall be of one piece with it, and you shall overlay it [the altar] with copper.
And thou shalt make its horns upon its four corners: the, horns shall be of it, they shall rise upward, and thou shalt cover it with brass.
27:3: Make its pots to remove [collect] its ashes, [also] its scoops, its basins, its flesh hooks, and its fire pans. Make all of its vessels out of copper.
And thou shalt make its pots to carry away its ashes and its shovels, and its basins, and its thuribles; all its vessels thou shalt make of brass.
27:4: Make for it a grate of copper netting. On the grate you shall make four copper rings on its four corners.
And thou shalt make for it a grate of network of brass, and upon the network four brass rings upon its four corners.
27:5: Place it under the rim of the altar, extending downward, so that the grate reaches the middle of the altar.

And thou shalt place it under the surroundings of the altar, beneath, that the network may be to the middle of the altar, that, if any fragment or fiery coal fall from the altar, it may fall upon the grate, and not touch the ground, and that the priests may take it from the grate, and replace it upon the altar.
27:6: Make poles for the altar, poles of acacia wood, and overlay them with copper.
And thou shalt make staves of sittin woods, and overlay them with brass;
27:7: Place its poles into the rings, and the poles shall be on the two sides of the altar when it is carried.
and thou shalt place the staves within the rings, and the staves shall be on the two sides of the altar in carrying the altar,
27:8: It should be a hollow structure constructed from boards. As it was shown to you on the mountain, so shall they make it.
hollow: (with) boards filled with dust shalt thou make it; according to what showed thee in the mountain, so shall they make.
27:9: You shall make the enclosure for the mishkon. On the south side there shall be curtains for the enclosure made of fine twined linen. It shall be one hundred amohs long on one side.
And thou shalt make the court of the tabernacle. For the southern side shall be hangings of fine linen twined; a hundred cubits the length for one side.
27:10: It shall have twenty pillars, and they shall have twenty copper sockets. The hooks and bands of the pillars shall be of silver.
And its pillars twenty, and their foundations twenty, of brass; the looks of the pillars, and their rods, of silver.
27:11: The same shall be on the north side. The curtains shall be one hundred amohs long, with twenty pillars and twenty copper sockets. The hooks and bands of the pillar shall be of silver.
And so for the northern side, for length, the hangings a hundred (cubits) long, and their pillars twenty, and their foundations twenty, of brass; the hooks of the pillars, and their rods, of silver.
27:12: For the width of the enclosure on the west side there shall be curtains of fifty amohs. They shall have ten pillars and ten sockets.
And for the breadth of the court on the western side, the hangings shall be fifty cubits; their columns ten and their foundations ten.
27:13: The width of the enclosure on the east side shall be fifty amohs.
And for the breadth of the eastern side eastward fifty cubits;
27:14: There shall be curtains fifteen amohs long on one flank [of the entrance]. They shall have three pillars and three sockets.
and fifteen cubits the hangings of the side, their pillars three and the their foundations three.
27:15: The other flank shall [also] have curtains of fifteen amohs. They [too] shall have three pillars and three sockets.
27:16: The entrance of the enclosure shall have a screen of twenty amohs. [It shall be made of] greenish-blue wool, dark red wool, crimson [colored] wool, and twined, fine linen. It shall be the work of an embroiderer. It [the screen] shall have four pillars and four sockets.
And for the door of the court shall be a veil of ten cubits of hyacinth, and purple, and crimson, and fine linen twined, of embroidered work; their pillars four, and their foundations four.
27:17: All the pillars around the enclosure shall have silver bands, and silver hooks, and copper sockets.
All the pillars of the court round about shall be united with silver rods; their hooks of silver, and their foundations of brass.
27:18: The length of the enclosure shall be one hundred amohs. The width shall be fifty by fifty amohs. The height [of the pillars holding up the curtains] of twisted fine linen shall be five amohs, and their sockets shall be [made] of copper.
The length of the court one hundred cubits, and the breadth fifty on the west and fifty on the east, and the height five cubits, of fine linen twined, and their foundations of brass.
27:19: All the vessels of the mishkon in all its service, all of its stakes and all the stakes of the enclosure, shall be made of copper.
All the vessels of the tabernacle in all its service, and all the pins of the court around, of brass.
27:20: You shall command the B’nei Yisrael and have them bring you clear olive oil, [made from olives that were] crushed for lighting, to keep the lamp burning constantly.
And thou shalt instruct the sons of Israel to bring the pure olive oil, beaten, for illumination, that the lamps may burn continually.
27:21: In the Tent of Meeting, outside the paroches, which is before the Testimony, Aharon and his sons shall arrange it [for the lamp to burn] from evening to morning before Adonoy. This is an everlasting statute for their generations of the B’nei Yisrael.

In the tabernacle of the covenant, without the veil that is before the testimony, Aharon and his sons shall set it in order from evening until morning before the Lord, an everlasting statute to your generations of the house of Israel.
28:1: And [now separate] and take unto you your brother, Aharon, and his sons with him, from among the B’nei Yisrael, to serve [before] Me [as kohanim]: Aharon, Nadav, Avihu, Elazar, and Isamar, the sons of Aharon.
And thou, bring near to thee Aharon thy brother, and his sons with him, from among the sons of Israel, to minister before Me: Aharon, Nadab, and Abihu, Elazar and Ithamar, the sons of Aharon.
28:2: Make sacred garments for your brother, Aharon, for honor and splendor.
And thou shalt make garments of holiness for Aharon thy brother, for glory and for praise.
28:3: Speak to all who are wise in heart, whom I have filled with the spirit of wisdom, and have them make Aharon’s garments, to sanctify him to serve [before] Me [as kohein].
And thou shalt speak with all who are wise of heart, and whom I have filled with the spirit of wisdom, that they make the vestments of Aharon to consecrate him to minister before Me.
28:4: These are the garments that they shall make: a breastplate, an eiphod, a robe, a checkered undershirt, a turban and a sash-belt. Have them make sacred garments for your brother Aharon, and for his sons, to serve [before] Me [as kohanim].

And these are the vestments they shall make: the breastplate and ephoda, and the robe, and the embroidered tunics, the mitres and girdles; and they shall make the holy garments for Aharon thy brother, and for his sons, to minister before Me.
28:5: They shall take the gold, the greenish-blue wool, the dark red wool the crimson [colored] wool, and the fine twined linen.
And they shall take from their treasures gold, and hyacinth, and purple, and crimson, and fine linen.
28:6: They shall make the eiphod out of gold, greenish-blue wool, dark red wool, crimson [colored] wool, and fine twined linen, the work of a craftsman.
And they shall make the ephod of hyacinth, and purple, and crimson, and fine linen, twined, the work of the artificer.
28:7: It shall have two shoulder straps attached to it, they shall be attached at its two corners [sides].
Two shoulder (pieces) shall it have, conjoined to its two sides, and (so) it shall be united.
28:8: The eiphod’s belt [that enhances it], which is on it, shall be made in the same manner [as the eiphod]—it shall be woven with it. [with] gold, greenish blue wool, dark red wool, crimson [colored] wool and fine twined linen.
And the ornamented girdle which is to be upon it shall be of the same work; of gold, hyacinth, purple, and crimson, and fine twined linen, shall it be.
28:9: Take two shoham [onyx] stones and engrave on them the names of the B’nei Yisrael.
And thou shalt take two gems of onyx, and engrave upon them the names of the sons of Israel.
28:10: Six of their names on the one stone, and the remaining six names on the second stone, in the order of their birth.
Six of their names shall be engraven upon one gem, and the six remaining names upon the second gem; they shall be set in the order of their nativity.
28:11: The work of a skilled [precious] stone engraver, like the engraving of a signet [ring] [written in script that is clear like they engrave a signet ring] shall you engrave the two stones with the names of the B’nei Yisrael. In gold settings shall you place them.

The engraved gems shall be the work of the artificer, engraven, and the engraving be distinct as the engraving of a ring; thou shalt engrave the two gems according to the names of the sons of Israel in their work round about; inset in gold shalt thou make them.
28:12: Set the two stones on the shoulder straps of the eiphod as remembrance stones for the B’nei Yisrael. Aharon shall bear their names before Adonoy, on his two shoulders as a remembrance.

And thou shalt fix the two gems upon the shoulders of the ephod, to be set for a memorial of righteousness for the sons, of Israel; and Aharon shall bear the names of the sons of Israel upon his two shoulders for a memorial.
28:13: And thou shalt make the sockets of gold.
28:14: and two chains of pure gold, you will make them for the ends, a braided work. and you will fasten the braided chain’s to the settings.
And two chains of pure gold, measured shalt thou make them, of twisted work, and insert the twisted chains in the sockets.
28:15: Make a breastplate of judgment, the work of a craftsman. Make it in the same manner you made the eiphod. [Out of] gold, greenish-blue wool, dark red wool, crimson [colored] wool and fine twined linen, shall you make it.

And thou shalt make the BREASTPLATE OF JUDGMENT, by which are made known the judgments that are hidden from the judges; and the order of the victories of their battles, and amends that are made for the judges; the work of the artificer; as the work of the ephod, thou shalt make it; of gold, hyacinth, and purple, and crimson, and fine linen twined, thou shalt make it.
28:16: It shall be a doubled square, a span in its length and a span in its width.
Square shall it be, doubled; a span its length, and a span its breadth.
28:17: Fill it [the breastplate settings] with fillings of [mounted] stones. Their shall be four rows of [precious] stones: [The first row:] An odem [ruby], pitda [topaz], and a barekes [emerald], [shall be placed on] the first row [one].

And thou shalt fill it with a fulness of precious stones: four rows of precious gems, answering to the four regions of the world. The first row, carnelian, topaz, carbuncle; and on them shall be engraven and expressed the names of the tribes Reuben, Shemeon, and Levi.
28:18: The second row: nofech [carbuncle], sapphire, and yahalom [diamond].
And the name of the second row, smaragd, and sapphire and chalcedony; and upon them shall be engraven and expressed the names of the three tribes, Jehuda, Dan, and Naphtali.
28:19: The third row: leshem [opal], shevo [agate], and achlomo [amethyst].
And the name of the third row, ligure, and agate, and amethyst; and upon them shall be written and expressed the names of three tribes, Gad, and Asher, and Issakar.
28:20: The fourth row: tarshish [chrysolite], shoham [onyx], and yoshfei [jasper]. [These stones] shall be placed in gold settings in their fullness.

And the name of the fourth row, chrysolite, onyx, and jasper; and upon them shall be written and expressed the names of three tribes, Zebulon, Joseph, and Benjamin. Set in gold shall they be, in their completeness.
28:21: These stones shall have on them the names of the B’nei Yisrael, twelve of them by their names, each one’s name [written in script that is clear like they engrave a signet ring] engraved as on a signet [ring], representing the twelve tribes.

And the jewels shall be taken according to the names of the sons of Israel, twelve are they according to their names, engraven and set forth as the engraving of a ring; the gem of each man according to his name: (so) shall they be for the twelve tribes.
28:22: Make [two] twisted end-chains for the breastplate, braided work of pure gold.
And thou shalt make upon the breastplate measured chains of twisted work of pure gold,
28:23: Make two gold ring’s for the breastplate, and set the two rings on the two [upper] corners [sides] for the breastplate.
and shalt make upon the breastplate two rings of pure gold, and put the two rings upon the two sides of the breastplate.
28:24: Place [attach] the two gold-braided chains on the two rings, at the corners [sides] of the breastplate.
And thou shalt put the two golden chains upon the two rings in the sides of the breastplate,
28:25: The two ends of the two braided chains [which are on its two sides], you shall place [attach] to the two settings, and place them on the shoulder straps of the eiphod toward its face.
and the two chains which are upon the two sides thou shalt put upon the two sockets, and set on the shoulders of the ephod against its front.
28:26: Make two gold rings and set them on the two [lower] corners [sides] of the breastplate, on its edge that is on the inner side of the eiphod.
And thou shalt make two golden rings, and fix them upon the two sides of the breastplate, in the border of it which is on the edge of the ephod inwardly.
28:27: Make two gold rings and place them on the two shoulder straps of the eiphod, on the bottom, toward its face, a gainst where they are joined, above the eiphod’s belt.
And thou shalt make (likewise) two golden chains, and fix them upon the two shoulders of the ephod beneath, towards its front, towards the place of its conjoinment above the girdle of the ephod;
28:28: They shall bind the [lower] rings of the breastplate to the [lower] rings of the eiphod with a cord of greenish-blue wool, so that it [the breastplate] remains against the eiphod’s belt, so that the breastplate does not move from the eiphod.

and they shall unite the breastplate with its rings to the rings of the ephod, with twined ribbon, of hyacinth, to be joined upon the girdle of the ephod, that the breastplate may not be removed from the ephod.
28:29: Aharon will thus carry the names of the B’nei Yisrael on the breastplate of judgment, over his heart, when he comes into the Holy [sanctuary], as a constant remembrance before Adonoy.
And Aharon shall bear the names of the sons of Israel upon his heart what time he entereth into the sanctuary for a good memorial before the Lord continually.
28:30: Place in the breastplate the Urim and Tumim, and they will be over Aharon’s heart when he comes before Adonoy. Aharon will carry the judgment of the B’nei Yisrael over his heart, before Adonoy always.

And thou shalt put upon the breastplate of judgment the Uraia, which illuminate their words, and manifest the hidden things of the house of Israel, and the Tumaia, which fulfil (or perfect) their work to the high priest, who seeketh instruction by them before the Lord; because in them is engraven and expressed the Great and Holy Name by which were created the three hundred and ten worlds, and which was engraven and expressed in the foundation stone wherewith the Lord of the world sealed up the mouth of the great deep at the beginning. Whosoever remembereth that holy name in the hour of necessity shall be delivered. And they shall be upon Aharon's heart in the time that he entereth before the Lord; and Aharon shall bear the judgment of the sons of Israel before the Lord continually.
28:31: Make the robe of the eiphod completely out of greenish-blue wool.
And thou shalt make the mantle-robe (mintar meila) of the ephod, of twined thread of hyacinth;
28:32: Its opening at the top shall be turned inward. Its opening shall have a border [encircling] all around, [this border shall be] of woven work, like there is around the opening of a coat of armor, so that it will not be torn.

and an orifice shall be in the middle of its upper part; a border shall be upon its opening round about its orifice, the work of the sewer; as the orifice of a coat of mail it shall be, that it may not be rent.
28:33: On its [lower] hem you shall make pomegranates of greenish-blue wool, dark red wool, and crimson [colored] wool—around its [lower] hem. There shall be gold bells between them, all around.
And thou shalt make upon the hem of it pomegranates of hyacinth, and purple, and crimson, upon its hem, round about, and bells of gold among them round about.
28:34: A gold bell and a pomegranate, a gold bell and a pomegranate, on the [lower] hem of the robe all around.
A golden bell, and a pomegranate of hyacinth and crimson; a golden bell, and a pomegranate of hyacinth and crimson upon the border of the robe round about; their number, seventy and one.
28:35: It shall be on Aharon when he performs [Divine] service. Its sound shall be heard when he comes into the Holy [sanctuary] in the presence of Adonoy, and when he comes out, so that he will not die.

And it shall be a vestment upon Aharon to minister, and its voice shall be heard at the time that he hath entered the holy place before the Lord, and at the time that he cometh out, that he die not by the flaming fire.
28:36: You shall make a diadem of pure gold, and engrave on it in the manner of a signet [ring] [script that is clear], “Holy unto Adonoy.”
And thou shalt make a plate (or crown) of pure gold, and engrave upon it with distinct engraving, HOLINESS TO THE LORD.
28:37: Set [fasten] it on a greenish-blue wool cord, so that it will be on the turban. It shall be near the front of the turban.
And thou shalt put it on a twined ribbon of hyacinth, to make amends for boldness of face; and it shall be on the mitre above the tephillin of the head in front of the mitre shall it be.
28:38: It shall be [worn] on Aharon’s forehead, and Aharon will carry [atone] the iniquity of the sacred offerings that the B’nei Yisrael consecrate for all their sacred gifts. It shall be on his forehead always to make them [the sacred-offerings] acceptable before Adonoy.

And it shall be in the front of Aharon's forehead, from time to time as it comes; and Aharon shall bear the iniquity of the consecrated things which the sons of Israel may consecrate; even of all their sacred gifts in which they have been insincere. And it shall be upon the front continually, for their reconciliation before the Lord.
28:39: Make the undershirt with checkered work of fine linen. Make the turban of fine linen. and the sash-belt shall be the work of an embroiderer.

And thou shalt weave the tunic of fine linen to expiate for the shedding of innocent blood; and shalt make the tiara of fine linen to expiate for the pride of their thoughts; and the girdle shalt thou make of the work of the embroiderer.
28:40: For Aharon’s sons, make undershirts, and [also] make sash-belts for them. Make turban-like hats for them, for honor and splendor.
